name: 1625 Prairie Avenue — Hugh J. McBirney's Tudor stone front, K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3½B brick dwelling (D), the south unit of the group'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: T-2432 (piece 1 of T-1869) refines the district draft (T-2335) in place under the same id from the house's one photograph, the Inland Architect plate of January 1890, 'Residence for Hugh J. McBirney' by Burling & Whitehouse (inland_architect_1890_01_mcbirney_residence), read against the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20, which controls the plan. The main body is rebuilt on the K01 frontage assembly at the sheet's own width (7.6 m, where the draft's fit had stopped at 6.75 m): a K02 rock-faced brownstone street front on K03 brick sides and rear, three storeys with the ground floor near grade, the north part two windows wide and the entrance at the south end of the front under one window a storey, as the photograph composes it; a slated K04/K05 hip with a pedimented dormer on the front marking where the photograph's steep wall gable stands. What the photograph shows and K01 cannot yet build — the full-width wall gable with its three lights and oculus, the mullioned and transomed lights, the frontispiece and its carved panel, the four-storey rear section stepping out to the south — is listed open in its match record (data/reference_views/house_1625_prairie/inland_architect_front.match.json) for T-2435. Everything not read is reconstructed and recorded as L-k01-1625-mcbirney-tudor-2432 (docs/RESEARCH/k01-1625-mcbirney-2432/README.md). T-2730 (piece 3 of T-2435) replaces the dormer with the photograph's coped wall gable — K01's shaped-gable slab with a straight outline in the front's stone, its three segment-headed lights and its oval light — raises the south wall's eave to the knee wall at 13.0 m, and stands the tall stack on the north party wall beside the gable; what that needed and did not read is L-k01-1625-mcbirney-wall-gable-2730. T-2752 (piece 1 of T-2731) reads the street windows off the photograph one by one (street_front_windows): the lower storeys' mullioned casements, two lights on the ground floor and two under a transom on the first, the four-light window over the door, the second floor's segment-headed sash off the columns below and the frontispiece's two narrow lights, on a plain plinth with no basement light (L-k01-1625-mcbirney-street-windows-2752). T-2753 (piece 2 of T-2731) builds the frontispiece (street_front_frontispiece): the front from 3.81 m to its south corner stands 0.10 m proud from grade to the hood mould over its four-light window at 7.05-7.30 m, quoined at both arrises, the door in a dressed surround under a carved panel; the lower windows' quoined surrounds and the photograph's one string course (L-k01-1625-mcbirney-frontispiece-2753). T-2820 (piece 1 of T-2754) builds the sheet's four-storey rear section as K01's rear_section: the step-out 1.3 m south of the main body over its rear 7.6 m in the K03 brick, its street face with the photograph's door and two windows, and over the rear part an attic of its own — steep slated faces to a curb at 17.3 m with the photograph's dormer on its street face, its south end wall carried up as a coped parapet to the rear stack — joined into the main roof, whose ridge dies into the attic's street face.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 1625 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1625 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The rear corner of the K01 main body at its north (low-v) side: the draft's origin moved 0.12 m north along its own frame, onto the north side of the 1911 sheet's traced main part (s20fp-1625-b1), the party wall with 1623, through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.607 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line, so v runs south.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1625-b1) in the lot frame: the stone front's face at 19.45 m from the rear of the trace (3.79 m from the street line), the north wall on the party line with 1623 at v -0.12 and the south wall at 7.48, so 19.45 m deep and 7.6 m along the front — the trace's own width, where the draft's 0.25 m cell fit stopped at 6.75 m. The four-storey rear section the sheet draws stepping 1.3 m further south over the rear 7.6 m (s20-1625-a1) is not part of this rectangle: a K01 footprint is one rectangle, and that section is built beside it as `rear_section` (T-2820).

stories.note: '3½B' on the 1911 sheet (the census's re-reading of the register's '3B', its half-storey glyph): three storeys over a basement and a half storey in the roof. The 1890 photograph agrees: three storeys of windows and an attic lit by three lights in the front gable.

construction.note: The photograph shows a street front of rock-faced coursed stone and a south side wall of brick; the 1911 sheet says only 'brick'. The Tribune's 'red stone' (quoted by chicagology, not yet a source record) is the stone.

principal_floor_m.note: The ground floor stands near grade: the photograph's door opens one low step over the walk, its foot at about 0.15 m (y 789 px, the dark of the doorway ending on its threshold), and its ground-floor sills sit about 1.2 m over grade (the Tribune's 'entrance at ground level', quoted by chicagology). T-2821: 0.15 m, one riser; T-2432 had read two low steps and built 0.45 m in three, which stood the door about 0.3 m too high.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, ground storey first (T-2821: the ground storey 3.45 m from the one-riser floor at 0.15 m, so the first floor stays at 3.6 m); the top storey's runs to the wall head. Through the photograph's camera (inland_architect_front.json, 38.6 px/m at the front's plane) the first-floor sills read at 4.15 m and the second-floor sills at 7.77 m over grade and the gable's lights at 11.5-13.3 m, so the floors at about 3.6, 7.2 and 11.0 m. T-2730: the photograph's south side wall rises to about 13 m before its eave and the south corner pier stops at 13.15 m (y 286 px), a knee wall under the attic; K01 has no attic storey, so the second floor's storey carries the knee wall and runs 5.8 m to a 13.0 m wall head (the attic floor at about 11.0 m is not built).

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front on its brick backing, as 1619's and 1634's.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house's.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays; the photograph's south wall is brick of a lighter tone than the stone.

stone_front.note: The photograph draws the front in rock-faced coursed stone of irregular course heights, with dressed quoined surrounds at the windows and a plain plinth; K02's brownstone, rock-faced, on a plain plinth (T-2821: one dressed course from grade to 0.26 m, the print's plinth top at y 785 px; it had been a rusticated base course under a 0.23 m coping to 0.48 m, the least a rusticated K02 base lays): the Tribune's 'red stone' (quoted by chicagology; 'Prentice' brownstone in its gloss) is a brown or red sandstone. The quoined window surrounds are built since T-2753 (street_front_windows.surrounds); the south corner's quoins are not built either, the K01 measure returning them only at its low-v end, which here is the party wall.

street_front_trim.note: Flat stone lintels over every front opening: the photograph's ground- and first-floor lights stand under flat heads in dressed surrounds. Its second-floor heads are segmental and the four-light window over the door carries a hood mould (T-2435).

wall_head.note: No cornice: the photograph carries the front up as a coped wall gable and runs the south wall's eave plain, with no brackets or entablature.

roof_form.note: A pitched roof: the photograph's main roof rises behind the front gable with its ridge running back from the street, slated, with a dormer on its south slope. K01's hip, its ridge along the plan's depth, stands behind the wall gable (shaped_gable, T-2730), whose slab its street slope dies into.

roof_pitch_deg.note: 45 degrees, the K01 contract's steepest hip: the hip is behind the gable, whose rakes are read at about 61 degrees (shaped_gable).

eave_overhang_m.note: T-2730: the photograph's south wall runs its eave plain with almost no projection, a few pixels (under 0.1 m) at the corner pier; 0.05 m, so that the gable slab, which K01 stands proud of the street fascia, keeps the street run of the eave's gutter inside it (the photograph shows no gutter across the front).

stair_tread_m.note: One low step up from the walk (T-2821; the floor's one riser), its going the kit's.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A shallow landing before a door set at grade.

entrance_bay.note: The door at the south end of the front, in the frontispiece, as the photograph shows it. 'north' is K01's name for the high-v end of the front; on the east side of the avenue the plan's v runs south, so that end is the south end on the ground.

front_bays.note: Three bays across the 7.6 m front, low v (north) to high v (south), read through the photograph's camera: the north part's two windows a storey (centred about 1.0 and 2.9-3.5 m from the party wall; the photograph's second-floor windows stand a little south of those under them, which K01's single bay line cannot follow) and the frontispiece's centre at 5.75 m, the door under one window a storey.

windows.why_not_ordinary: the oriel's cheek lights: the print's west cheek is 0.48 m deep and its light about 0.37 m across (x 506-517 px)

bays.note: T-2846: the oriel the photograph shows on the main south wall just in front of the rear section (x 504-527 px), read through the re-solved camera (inland_architect_front.json). A box on the wall, not canted: its west cheek faces the plate (x 505-519.5 px) and its long south face recedes beside it (x 519.5-527.5); only a cheek 0.48 m deep puts both of the west cheek's edges at one depth (8.16 m behind the front), and the south face's far end then stands at 9.45 m, so the oriel is 1.29 m along the wall, centred 8.8 m back. Its far end hides the wall from there to the rear section's corner, which is why it seems to abut it. Heights at the cheek's scale (30.05 px/m): the foot of its apron about 2.3 m (y 718), its lights' sills about 3.5 m (y 681) and their heads about 5.5 m (y 621), the moulded cornice to about 5.8 m (y 613); nothing shows over it, so its roof is low. Built as K08's oriel on the first floor (3.6 m), a storey of 2.0 m to its wall top under K08's eaves (to about 5.8 m), on five corbel courses, the most a 0.48 m reach may carry and still bear 0.08 m on the wall (to 2.6 m, about 10 px over the print's foot); one light in each cheek and one in the south face, two-over-two sash as the kit's oriel, 1.85 m tall from 0.05 m over its floor. Reconstructed: the plan's square corners (the print cannot tell a square cheek from a slightly canted one), the east cheek and its light (hidden behind the oriel), the panes, the timber of its walls (the print reads joinery: thin framing round the lights, a moulded cornice, a panelled apron), the corbel courses for the apron, and the low copper hip (L-k01-1625-oriel-2846). Earlier: none, the front being flat (T-2435), which still holds for the front.

side_bays.note: None: the house's NORTH side wall (K01's 'south', low v) is the party wall with 1623, built blank, as the sheet draws the group attached.

north_bays.note: Windows in the house's SOUTH side wall (K01's 'north', high v; s from the front corner), toward the open ground the sheet leaves south of 1625: the photograph shows single windows a storey along the main part's south wall, the nearest about 4 m behind the front. Their places further back are reconstructed. T-2820: the two that stood in the rear 7.6 m (s 14.3 and 17.6) are gone, the rear section standing over that part of the wall.

rear_bays.note: Two windows a storey in the rear wall; no picture shows it.

rear_wings.note: None: the sheet's four-storey rear section (s20-1625-a1) stands beside the main body's rear part, stepping out to the south, which a K01 rear wing (behind the main body, inside its width) cannot; since T-2820 it is built as `rear_section`.

rear_section.note: T-2820: the 1911 sheet's four-storey rear section (s20-1625-a1), the rear 7.6 m of the trace stepping 1.3 m further south than the main body (the trace's south line at -3028.0 to -3028.4 where the main part's runs at -3027.0 to -3027.2), built beside the main body's rear part on its south side (K01's north wall, high v): the step-out's three walls in the K03 brick to the main wall head, and over the whole rear part an attic of its own. The photograph (inland_architect_front.json) shows it behind the main body's south wall: a narrow face toward the street in darker brick with a door at its foot and one window a storey over it, its cornice meeting the main south eave at the same height (both at y 482-488 px where they meet), and over it a slated attic with a dormer on its street face and the south end wall carried up as a lit brick face to a stack. The camera's depth is soft that far back (its own solve: +-3 m), so heights are read against the cornice, set at the main wall head's 13.0 m where the photograph's cornice meets the main eave, and the horizon (y 733 px at 1.6 m): about 0.046 m a pixel. On that scale the windows stand 3.66-6.65 m and 9.02-11.48 m, the door's head about 1.7 m (it is built 2.1 m tall from grade, the fence hiding its foot), the dormer's sill 13.85 m and its sash's head 16.3 m, and the attic's top line, its curb, 17.3 m: a 4.3 m lower face. Widths are the sheet's: the face is 1.3 m, so its windows are the contract's narrowest sash (0.75 m) and its dormer 0.84 m, centred, where the photograph's face reads about 50 px across (about 2.2 m on that scale) and its lights about half of it; that disagreement is recorded open in the match record. Reconstructed: the lower faces' 75-degree pitch, the attic's 15-degree top over the curb (the photograph cannot see it), the 0.3 m cornice, the end walls carried up as coped parapets at the party wall and the step-out's outer face (the photograph shows the south one; the north one is the party wall's), and the step-out's outer and rear walls left blank (the photograph shows the outer one lit and windowless; no picture shows the rear) (L-k01-1625-rear-section-2820). T-2846: re-ruled on the camera re-solved on the south wall's level lines (inland_architect_front.json). The face's width is 1.8 m, the print's, not the sheet's 1.3: the face stands parallel to the plate, so its width against its own heights does not depend on the camera at all, and on the re-solved camera (27.3 px/m at the face, 11.85 m behind the front as the sheet sets it) the face's 48 px (x 528-576) is 1.8 m, its rear corner landing at x 606 against the print's 608 (a 1.3 m face would end at x 564). The sheet's trace steps 0.8-1.4 m (its south lines at -3028.0 to -3028.4 against -3027.0 to -3027.2), within a traced line's width of a 1:600 sheet; the photograph is the better measure. Across the wider face the print's openings stand toward the main wall's corner, not centred: the door's right jamb at x 557 (it is built 0.85 m wide at s 0.63 m, its left jamb the kit's 0.2 m pier from the corner, where the print's dark runs into the corner's shadow at x 528), the lower window x 534-557 (0.88 m at s 0.64), the upper x 536-556 (0.77 m at s 0.64), and the dormer's sash centred at x 547 (8.3 m from the party wall). The door is a door at grade, not an areaway's: on the re-solved camera its head (y 730, the top of a transom light over the leaf) reads 1.9-2.1 m over grade for an eye 1.3-0.5 m high, where the old camera put it on its own horizon at 1.7 m; the built 2.1 m head stands within about 3 px. The heights on this face still stand on the main eave at 13.0 m, which the re-solved camera reads at 10.9 m: that, the windows', the dormer's and the curb's heights and the door's transom are T-2847's.

sash_by_storey.note: Storey by storey, the photograph's north-part windows through its camera: ground-floor lights 1.1-2.7 m over grade, first-floor 4.15-6.4 m, second-floor 7.8-10.1 m. Since T-2752 the street front's windows are street_front_windows'; these rows size the side, rear and north walls' sash, at the contract's single sash widths (0.75-1.15 m). T-2821: the ground storey's sill 0.96 m over its floor, the floor now at 0.15 m, so the side wall's ground-floor sills stay at 1.11 m.

street_front_windows.note: T-2752: every street window read off the photograph through its camera (data/reference_views/house_1625_prairie/inland_architect_front.json: level and square to the front, 38.6 px/m at the front's plane, grade at y 795 px, the party wall at x 140 px), each opening's stone edges and its sill and head on 4x crops of the print: s = (x - 140) / 38.6 m from the north party wall, height = (795 - y) / 38.6 m. Ground floor: two windows in the north part, each two tall casement lights on a stone mullion, 1.19-2.59 m, centred at 0.94 and 2.88 m, 1.04 and 1.17 m across (the print gives the south one of each pair a little wider, at both storeys). First floor: the same two, each two lights on a mullion under a stone transom about a third down, 4.14-6.40 m; over the door the four-light window, mullioned and transomed alike, 2.18 m across at 5.78 m, 4.25-6.58 m (read at the front's plane: its frontispiece stands slightly proud, which T-2753 weighs). Second floor: two one-over-one sash under segmental heads, off the columns below, at 1.15 and 3.45 m, 0.94 and 1.02 m across, from 7.74 and 7.87 m to crowns at 9.97 and 10.18 m; and the frontispiece's two narrow segment-headed two-over-two lights at 5.38 and 6.39 m, 0.62 m across, 8.84-10.42 m. The glazing bars are the K06 kit's: the print shows the lower windows' lights in small panes but cannot say whether on lead or wood. Each edge is good to about a pixel, 0.03 m. The plinth: plain, with no basement light in it (the 1911 sheet's basement is lit elsewhere, or not at the front); its top is the K02 base's least, one 0.25 m course under the 0.23 m coping, 0.48 m, where the print's smooth plinth band stands about 0.26 m over the walk (y 785 px). T-2753: the belts and the surrounds, read the same way. The photograph runs one string course across the whole front, its top under the first floor's sills: 3.94-4.09 m in the north part (y 637-643 px) and about 4.04-4.22 m on the frontispiece, where its face is nearer the camera; built 3.96-4.14 m, in place of K01's own two belts (3.40-3.60 and 7.05-7.20 m), of which the print shows neither. The ground and first floors' windows stand in dressed surrounds: smooth jamb stones, wider and narrower in turn up the courses (about 0.2-0.3 m on 3x crops), and a dressed lintel over the head running about 0.1-0.25 m past the jambs (the ground floor's 2.64-3.03 m, y 678-693 px, x 147-200 px over a window at x 156-196 px); built as the coursing's own stones dressed and laid flush, 0.18 and 0.30 m in turn, and a 0.35 m lintel course 0.18 m past each jamb. The second floor's segmental sash show no such surround. T-2821: base_top_m 0.26, the print's plain plinth (y 785 px), laid as one dressed course.

street_front_frontispiece.note: T-2753: the frontispiece read off the photograph through its camera (inland_architect_front.json: 38.6 px/m at the front's plane, grade at y 795 px, the party wall at x 140 px; s = (x - 140) / 38.6 m) on 3x crops of the print. Its north arris is a column of dressed quoins, long and short in turn, at x 287-298 px from the plinth to the hood (s 3.81 m; the quoins about 0.28 and 0.45 m, built 0.25 and 0.42 m); its south arris is the front's south corner, quoined the same way (x 417-437 px). It stands proud of the north part, but the print is taken square to the front and cannot measure by how much: 0.10 m is reconstructed, 'slightly proud' as T-2752 read it. Its top is the hood mould over the four-light window, a projecting weathered course across the frontispiece's whole width, y 513-523 px, 7.05-7.30 m, built 0.08 m past the frontispiece's face and its north arris (reconstructed: the print shows its shadow, not its depth). The door stands in a dressed surround, jambs about 0.35-0.45 m wide (x 320-337 and 385-398 px) and a lintel 0.47 m deep (y 675-693 px); built a 0.35 m band round the door with its lintel 2.64-3.11 m, the print's (T-2821: the door brought down to the print's 2.64 m head, door_clear_height_m; until then K07's door stood its head at 3.15 m and the lintel at 3.45 m). Over it, the carved panel: a square of carved figures about a cartouche, x 343-375 px, 0.83 m across, centred s 5.67 m, 3.16-4.02 m in the print; built 0.83 m across between the surround's lintel and the string course, 3.11-3.96 m, 0.85 m tall (T-2821; 0.51 m while the door stood high), a raised moulded border 0.04 m proud with a raised oval cartouche inside it standing for the carving, whose figures are not modelled. L-k01-1625-mcbirney-frontispiece-2753.

roof_covering.note: Slate: the photograph's roof slopes and the rear section's mansard read as slate. The Tribune's 'Roman tile' (quoted by chicagology) may be the roof or the walling; K04's terracotta tile is documented-only, so it waits for a source record.

chimneys.note: Two brick stacks: one against the north party wall beside the gable, where the photograph's tall stack rises left of its north rake — solved through the photograph's camera (eye 17.45 m before the face, f 674 px) from its edges at x 180 and 217 px, it stands about 1.6 m behind the gable's face and 1.0 m along the front from the party wall, its top at about 17.7 m, the ridge's 16.8 m and 0.9 (T-2730; built 0.3 m in from the party wall, the K01 rule for a stack standing in a hip); and the photograph's rear stack, which T-2820 stands in the rear section's south end wall where it rises past the attic: about 4.4 m from the rear wall by its place along that wall's head line (about x 580-602 px of the wall's 577-610), 1.0 m along it and 0.6 m through it, its outer face the step-out's; its top at 19.6 m, about 1.5 m over the attic's ridge, the height it stands over the wall's head line where it leaves it (about 30 px at the section's scale). Its depth through the wall and its plan are reconstructed (L-k01-1625-rear-section-2820). T-2846: the rear stack moved out with the step-out's outer face (now 1.8 m past the south wall, v 9.4), its outer face still the step-out's (v 8.8-9.4): on the re-solved camera it spans x 573-592 against the print's 577-605; its depth along the wall is T-2847's.

rainwater.note: Half-round gutters and round downpipes at the front's two corners: the photograph shows a downpipe down the front's north edge, against the neighbour, and one at the south corner. T-2753: the south one stands on the open south side wall (the K01 measure's north wall: v runs south on this side of the avenue) 0.15 m behind the front corner, where the print draws it (x 435-438 px, just past the corner at x 433), clear of the frontispiece and its hood.

window_kit.note: The street windows from the photograph's kinds (T-2752): the lower storeys' mullioned casements, two lights on the ground floor and two under a transom on the first, the four-light window over the door, the second floor's one-over-one segmental sash and the frontispiece's narrow two-over-two segmental lights. The side, rear and north walls, which the photograph does not show or shows only in raking light, keep the K06 kit's two-over-two sash.

entrance_kit.note: K07's panelled door at the head of a short stoop; the front yard is 3.78 m, the sheet's front at 19.45 m against the street line at 23.24 m. The photograph's doorway is flat-headed in a dressed surround under a carved panel (T-2435).

door_clear_height_m.note: T-2821: the doorway read off the photograph through its camera (inland_architect_front.json: 38.6 px/m at the front's plane, grade at y 795 px) on a 4x crop: its dark opening runs from the threshold at y 789 px (0.15 m, the floor's one riser) to its flat head at y 693 px (2.64 m), so 2.49 m clear; 1.22 m across (x 337-385 px), the K01 door's 1.20 m. K01's 2.70 m stood the head at 3.15 m. The leaf is K07's panelled door at that size: the print shows the doorway black and cannot say how its leaf is panelled.

shaped_gable.note: T-2730: the photograph carries the whole front up as a steep coped wall gable in the front's rock-faced stone, read through its camera (38.6 px/m at the front's plane, grade y 795 px): the apex at 18.85 m (y 67 px), the rakes at about 60 (south) and 66 (north) degrees, so a straight outline from 3.2 m either side of the centre at the 13.0 m ledge to the apex (61 degrees); the south rake lands on the corner pier's flat top at 13.15 m, which the ledge between the outline and the eave's corner stands for, with no kneeler pinnacle and no finial. Three one-over-one lights under segmental stone heads, 11.53-13.34 m over grade (y 350-280 px), about 0.6 m of glass each in a 0.66 m opening, their centres 0.94 m apart (x 239, 275 and 311 px); an oval light near the apex, its glass about 0.45 by 0.85 m (17 by 32 px) centred at 15.56 m (y 194 px), in a dressed ring about 0.09 m wide, its tracery built as a cross of bars. The coping, 0.3 m, is the photograph's dressed stone along both rakes. Not read: the slab's thickness, and its foot at 11.22 m, where the gable's face steps 0.25 m proud of the wall below it as a band under the lights' sills (the photograph's sill course there; K01 stands the slab proud of the street fascia and its gutter, which the photograph does not show across the front), and the gable's centre, built on the front's (3.8 m from the party wall) where the photograph's apex and middle light stand about 0.3 m (12 px) north of it. L-k01-1625-mcbirney-wall-gable-2730.
